item.title: xiaozhangup/Oh-My-McDonald: A conversational AI Skill based on McDonald's official MCP, supporting meal recommendations, store price comparison, coupon lookup, nutrition calculation, and exploration logs, and generating voxel-style share images with Python.
item.description: Oh-My-McDonald is a conversational AI Skill built on McDonald's official MCP, offering meal recommendations, store price comparison, coupon lookup, nutrition calculation, and exploration logs. It also generates voxel-style share images with Python. Why it matters: Shows how a company's official MCP can power a conversational AI skill for meal, price, and coupon questions.

item.title: heterodoxin/AbliteratedOutTheBox: llama.cpp fork that abliterates at inference
item.description: AbliteratedOutTheBox is a llama.cpp fork that makes supported AI models answer harmful prompts they would normally refuse, changing behavior at inference time without altering the saved weights. Why it matters: A tool that strips refusals from supported models is relevant to AI safety and cybersecurity readers.

item.title: wahaha-potato/mcd-coupon-xray: Anyone can claim the Maimai Province coupons, but claiming one doesn't mean the store downstairs will accept it. After claiming them all with one click, it checks each store to see which coupon can actually be redeemed, calculates the net price after the coupon, and directly answers 'which store to go to, which coupon to use, and how much you save.' Based on the McDonald's MCP.
item.description: A Python tool built on McDonald's MCP that claims Maimai Province coupons at once, then finds which store accepts which coupon and the net price.

item.description: M Meal Buddy is a TypeScript skill that suggests meal pairings using McDonald's MCP real-time menu and nutrition data; an online demo is live.

item.title: Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats.
item.description: A study found that when forced to pick, Grok 4.7 recommended the Republican candidate in 92% of answers, while GPT-6.1 Sol picked the Democrat in 97%. The two agreed less than 10% of the time across nearly 500 races. Why it matters: Suggests AI chatbots may not be politically neutral when asked for voting advice.
